explain.entry:
Pattern: -(으)ㄹ게요
Meaning: I will (a promise or decision, for the listener)
Note: Only with I/we. Use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for plans that don't involve the listener.
Example: 제가 먼저 연락할게요. = I'll contact you first
Example: 내일 다시 올게요. = I'll come again tomorrow

Pattern: -아/어 보다
Meaning: To try doing something
Note: Past form -아/어 봤어요 means you have tried it before.
Example: 이 노래 한번 들어 보세요. = Try listening to this song once
Example: 한국 음식을 만들어 봤어요. = I tried making Korean food

Pattern: -기로 하다
Meaning: To decide to
Example: 올해부터 운동하기로 했어요. = I decided to exercise starting this year
Example: 우리 주말에 만나기로 했어요. = We decided to meet on the weekend

Pattern: -(으)면서
Meaning: While (doing two things at the same time)
Note: The same person does both actions.
Example: 음악을 들으면서 공부해요. = I study while listening to music
Example: 커피를 마시면서 이야기했어요. = We talked while drinking coffee

Pattern: -는 동안
Meaning: During / While
Example: 제가 자는 동안 비가 왔어요. = It rained while I was sleeping
Example: 기다리는 동안 책을 읽었어요. = I read a book while I was waiting

Pattern: -(으)ㄹ까 봐
Meaning: Worried that / In case
Example: 늦을까 봐 택시를 탔어요. = I took a taxi because I was worried I'd be late
Example: 비가 올까 봐 우산을 가져왔어요. = I brought an umbrella in case it rains

Pattern: -아/어야 하다
Meaning: To have to
Example: 내일 일찍 일어나야 해요. = I have to wake up early tomorrow
Example: 이 약은 하루에 세 번 먹어야 해요. = You have to take this medicine three times a day

Pattern: -지 말다
Meaning: Don't (negative command)
Note: -지 마세요 is polite, -지 마 is casual.
Example: 걱정하지 마세요. = Don't worry
Example: 울지 마. = Don't cry

Pattern: (으)로
Meaning: Direction or means
Example: 지하철로 가요. = I go by subway.

Pattern: 한테
Meaning: To someone
Example: 친구한테 문자를 보냈어요. = I sent a text to my friend.

Pattern: 부터
Meaning: Starting point (time)
Example: 아홉 시부터 일해요. = I work from nine.

Pattern: 까지
Meaning: Until / Up to
Example: 밤늦게까지 공부했어요. = I studied until late at night.

Pattern: -ㄹ 지/ 을 지
Meaning: whether
Note: Use -ㄹ지 말지 when expressing indecision.
Example: 비가 올지 안 올지 모르겠어요. = I don't know whether it'll rain or not
Example: 말할지 말지 모르겠어요 = I don't know whether to say it or not

mcq.source:
Sentences
1. 오늘 하루도 수고 많았어요 = You worked hard today too.
People say it at the end of the day, like "good job today".
2. 나 너 때문에 진짜 웃었어 = I really laughed because of you.
3. 밥 먹었어? = Did you eat?
A way to say "how are you" to friends.
4. 이거 보고 너 생각나서 샀어 = I saw this and thought of you, so I bought it.
5. 주말에 시간 있으면 영화 보러 갈래? = If you have time this weekend, want to go see a movie?
6. 괜찮아, 다 잘될 거야 = It's okay, everything will be fine.

mcq.korean: 길이 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같아요
mcq.english: The road is jammed, so I think I'll be a little late
mcq.source:
Sentences
7. 길이 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같아요 = The road is jammed, so I think I'll be a little late.
8. 날씨가 너무 추워서 밖에 나가기 싫어요 = It's so cold that I don't want to go outside.
9. 사진 잘 나왔네요 = The photo came out well.
10. 요즘 이 노래만 계속 들어요 = These days I keep listening to this song only.
11. 너무 졸려서 커피를 두 잔이나 마셨어요 = I was so sleepy that I drank two whole cups of coffee.
12. 우리 언제 한번 밥 먹어요 = Let's eat together sometime.
Often polite small talk, not a real plan.

mcq.english: To take out / To wrap up
mcq.source:
At the café and the restaurant
1. 메뉴판 = Menu
메뉴판 좀 주세요. = Can I have the menu, please?
2. 계산하다 = To pay (the bill)
오늘은 제가 계산할게요. = I'll pay today.
계산해 주세요 = The bill, please
3. 포장하다 = To take out / To wrap up
남은 음식 포장해 주세요. = Please wrap up the leftovers.
Used at restaurants: 포장이요! = To go!
4. 맵다 = To be spicy
떡볶이가 너무 매워요. = The tteokbokki is too spicy.
매워요
5. 싱겁다 = To be bland
국이 좀 싱거워요. = The soup is a bit bland.
6. 짜다 = To be salty
이 김치는 너무 짜요. = This kimchi is too salty.

At the café and the restaurant
7. 달다 = To be sweet
케이크가 생각보다 안 달아요. = The cake isn't as sweet as I thought.
8. 맛집 = Popular restaurant
여기 유명한 맛집이에요. = This is a famous restaurant.
People post 맛집 photos on Instagram
9. 예약하다 = To reserve / To book
일곱 시로 예약했어요. = I made a reservation for seven.
10. 자리 = Seat / Spot
창가 자리 있어요? = Is there a window seat?
11. 남기다 = To leave (food)
음식을 남기지 마세요. = Don't leave food on your plate.

구워요

컵에 물을 부어 주세요. = Please pour water into the cup.
부어요
16. 줄을 서다 = To stand in line
사람들이 줄을 서 있어요. = People are standing in line.
17. 영수증 = Receipt
영수증 필요하세요? = Do you need a receipt?
18. 배고프다 = To be hungry

Casual exaggeration: 죽겠어요 = I could die
19. 진하다 = To be strong (drink) / To be thick

mcq.english: To feel hurt / To feel let down
mcq.source:
Feelings
1. 설레다 = To be excited / To have butterflies
내일 여행 갈 생각에 너무 설레요. = I'm so excited thinking about tomorrow's trip.
2. 서운하다 = To feel hurt / To feel let down
내 생일을 잊어버려서 좀 서운했어. = I felt a bit hurt that you forgot my birthday.
3. 귀엽다 = To be cute
강아지가 너무 귀여워요! = The puppy is so cute!
귀여워
4. 외롭다 = To be lonely
혼자 살면 가끔 외로워요. = When you live alone, you sometimes feel lonely.

Feelings
5. 무섭다 = To be scary / To be scared
이 영화 진짜 무서워요. = This movie is really scary.
6. 짜증나다 = To be annoyed
아침부터 버스를 놓쳐서 짜증났어. = I missed the bus this morning, so I was annoyed.
7. 그립다 = To miss / To long for
고향 음식이 그리워요. = I miss the food from my hometown.
8. 힘들다 = To be hard / To be tiring
오늘 일이 너무 힘들었어요. = Work was really hard today.
9. 행복하다 = To be happy
너랑 있으면 행복해. = I'm happy when I'm with you.

Sentences
1. 오늘 하루도 수고 많았어요 = You worked hard today too.
People say it at the end of the day, like "good job today".
2. 나 너 때문에 진짜 웃었어 = I really laughed because of you.
3. 밥 먹었어? = Did you eat?
A way to say "how are you" to friends.
4. 이거 보고 너 생각나서 샀어 = I saw this and thought of you, so I bought it.
5. 주말에 시간 있으면 영화 보러 갈래? = If you have time this weekend, want to go see a movie?
6. 괜찮아, 다 잘될 거야 = It's okay, everything will be fine.

Grammar: week 14
My Korean notes. One rule: Korean = English.
1. -(으)ㄹ게요
Meaning: I will (a promise or decision, for the listener)
제가 먼저 연락할게요. = I'll contact you first.
내일 다시 올게요. = I'll come again tomorrow.
Explanation: Only with I/we. Use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for plans that don't involve the listener.
2. -아/어 보다
Meaning: To try doing something
이 노래 한번 들어 보세요. = Try listening to this song once.
한국 음식을 만들어 봤어요. = I tried making Korean food.
Explanation: Past form -아/어 봤어요 means you have tried it before.
3. -기로 하다
Meaning: To decide to
올해부터 운동하기로 했어요. = I decided to exercise starting this year.
우리 주말에 만나기로 했어요. = We decided to meet on the weekend.
4. -(으)면서
Meaning: While (doing two things at the same time)
음악을 들으면서 공부해요. = I study while listening to music.
커피를 마시면서 이야기했어요. = We talked while drinking coffee.
Explanation: The same person does both actions.
5. -는 동안
Meaning: During / While
제가 자는 동안 비가 왔어요. = It rained while I was sleeping.
기다리는 동안 책을 읽었어요. = I read a book while I was waiting.
6. -(으)ㄹ까 봐
Meaning: Worried that / In case
늦을까 봐 택시를 탔어요. = I took a taxi because I was worried I'd be late.
비가 올까 봐 우산을 가져왔어요. = I brought an umbrella in case it rains.
7. -아/어야 하다
Meaning: To have to
내일 일찍 일어나야 해요. = I have to wake up early tomorrow.
이 약은 하루에 세 번 먹어야 해요. = You have to take this medicine three times a day.
8. -지 말다
Meaning: Don't (negative command)
걱정하지 마세요. = Don't worry.
울지 마. = Don't cry.
Explanation: -지 마세요 is polite, -지 마 is casual.

Main function

Direction or means

한테
To someone

부터
Starting point (time)
아홉 시부터 일해요. — I work from nine.
까지
Until / Up to
밤늦게까지 공부했어요. — I studied until late at night.

Grammar: week 14
My Korean notes. One rule: Korean = English.
1. -(으)ㄹ게요
Meaning: I will (a promise or decision, for the listener)
제가 먼저 연락할게요. = I'll contact you first.
내일 다시 올게요. = I'll come again tomorrow.
Explanation: Only with I/we. Use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for plans that don't involve the listener.
2. -아/어 보다
Meaning: To try doing something

한국 음식을 만들어 봤어요. = I tried making Korean food.
Explanation: Past form -아/어 봤어요 means you have tried it before.
3. -기로 하다
Meaning: To decide to
올해부터 운동하기로 했어요. = I decided to exercise starting this year.
우리 주말에 만나기로 했어요. = We decided to meet on the weekend.
4. -(으)면서
Meaning: While (doing two things at the same time)
음악을 들으면서 공부해요. = I study while listening to music.
커피를 마시면서 이야기했어요. = We talked while drinking coffee.
Explanation: The same person does both actions.

Meaning: During / While

기다리는 동안 책을 읽었어요. = I read a book while I was waiting.

Meaning: Worried that / In case
늦을까 봐 택시를 탔어요. = I took a taxi because I was worried I'd be late.

Travel
7. 열다 = To open

8. 묻다 = To ask
길을 물어봤어요. = I asked for directions.

(Korean = English) or its notes. Use / for synonyms: any of them counts as right.
Vocabulary
1. 근처 = Nearby
이 근처에는 카페가 없어요. = There are no cafes in this vicinity.
학교가 집 근처에 있어요. = The school is nearby my house.
2. 안 = Inside
가방 안에 있어요. = It's inside of the bag.
3. 가장 / 제일 = The most / best
4. 걷다 = To walk
걸어요
걸을 거야
5. 혼자 = Alone, on one's own
저 혼자 살아요 = I live alone
혼자서 = By oneself
6. 챙기다 = To take (Important no forget)
Use it like "dont forget to take this..." because is important
Sentences
1. 피곤하니까 집에 갈래요 = Since I am tired, I want to go home.
2. 비가 오니까 우산을 챙기세요 = Because it's raining, take an umbrella.
Use 으니까 because we cannot use 어서 in commands.
1. -ㄹ 지/ 을 지
Meaning: whether
비가 올지 안 올지 모르겠어요. = I don't know whether it'll rain or not.
말할지 말지 모르겠어요 = I don't know whether to say it or not
Explanation: Use -ㄹ지 말지 when expressing indecision.
2. -네요
Meaning: A reaction to something you see or feel right now
비싸네요
좋네요

Sentences
1. 피곤하니까 집에 갈래요 = Since I am tired, I want to go home.
2. 비가 오니까 우산을 챙기세요 = Because it's raining, take an umbrella.
Use 으니까 because we cannot use 어서 in commands.

is_grounded.answer: Because it's raining, take an umbrella
is_grounded.source:
Sentences from dramas and social media
My Korean notes. One rule: Korean = English.
Sentences
1. 오늘 하루도 수고 많았어요 = You worked hard today too.
People say it at the end of the day, like "good job today".
2. 나 너 때문에 진짜 웃었어 = I really laughed because of you.
3. 밥 먹었어? = Did you eat?
A way to say "how are you" to friends.
4. 이거 보고 너 생각나서 샀어 = I saw this and thought of you, so I bought it.
5. 주말에 시간 있으면 영화 보러 갈래? = If you have time this weekend, want to go see a movie?
6. 괜찮아, 다 잘될 거야 = It's okay, everything will be fine.
Sentences
7. 길이 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같아요 = The road is jammed, so I think I'll be a little late.
8. 날씨가 너무 추워서 밖에 나가기 싫어요 = It's so cold that I don't want to go outside.
9. 사진 잘 나왔네요 = The photo came out well.
10. 요즘 이 노래만 계속 들어요 = These days I keep listening to this song only.
11. 너무 졸려서 커피를 두 잔이나 마셨어요 = I was so sleepy that I drank two whole cups of coffee.
12. 우리 언제 한번 밥 먹어요 = Let's eat together sometime.
Often polite small talk, not a real plan.
Sentences
13. 혹시 이 근처에 편의점 있어요? = Is there a convenience store near here, by any chance?
14. 생일 축하해, 행복한 하루 보내 = Happy birthday, have a happy day.
15. 이 옷 나한테 잘 어울려? = Do these clothes suit me?
16. 오랜만에 친구를 만나서 정말 좋았어요 = It was really nice to meet a friend after a long time.
17. 비 오는 날에는 집에서 쉬는 게 최고예요 = On rainy days, resting at home is the best.
18. 그 사람 목소리를 들으면 마음이 편해져요 = When I hear that person's voice, I feel at ease.
Sentences
19. 할 수 있어, 포기하지 마 = You can do it, don't give up.
20. 다음에 또 놀러 오세요 = Please come visit again next time.
